Social support was measured using the Social Support Survey
(MOS), French version. It is an eight-item survey assessing the

The usefulness of the BYP-BC intervention was measured using a
questionnaire designed specifically for the study. It was an eight-
item survey assessing the extent to which each component of the
yoga intervention was useful (0 = Not at all, 4 = Extremely).
An intention-to-treat analysis using multiple imputations was
employed in order to handle missing data and include every ran-
domized participant [37]. Multiple imputation consists in filling
missing data by estimating their values including the standard
error for each imputation. As suggested by Bodner [38], the number
of imputations should match the percentage of missing data. After
analyzing the percentage of missing data and concluding it was
missing at random, 21 imputations were carried out.
